_readme: The warden's opening, and the game's premise. Named by the map AND opened by the hooks:
on_map_entered forces it the first time the player stands in the village, because a
play-test found the oil, never found the key, and was never told either existed.
Its `greet` node sets met_the_warden, which is what stops the hook replaying it. A node
flag lands when the line is SHOWN, so a conversation nobody saw is one they are still owed.
Every fact a player needs to take the first step is in `why`: that there is a key, that it
is west in the hollow, and that it is under the one bush down there. That last one used to
be stated NOWHERE - the stash is an unmarked object standing on scenery.

greet.speaker: Warden
greet.text: You want to know why the gate is barred. I barred it. Something took the keep eleven years ago, and I could not take it back.

why.speaker: Warden
why.text: The key went west into the hollow, under the roots of the one bush down there. What nests beside it now is why nobody has fetched it.

good.speaker: Warden
good.text: Then you are already doing more than I have in a decade. Mind the smith in the town south of here - she keeps something for cuts.

fair.speaker: Warden
fair.text: It is. And it will still be my problem tomorrow, when you have run out of other things to do.
